excerpt: Delightful project orchestration environment (IDE) for software engineering with AI agents. Bring your with subscription. - AltharIDE/althar
content_html:
Stop babysitting tabs and terminals.
Tell Althar's coordinator what you want. It puts agents to work, can have a model from another lab review them, and brings you back finished work, with the proof.

Download · Website · Get started · Contributing

Open source · Your own agents and plans · Runs on your computer · macOS, Windows and Linux

Features

Coordinator

Tell it what you want, as you would a project manager. It knows your repositories, rules and past decisions, splits the work into tasks, picks an agent and a model to lead each, and starts them unless you change or hold it.

Review by another lab

A model from another lab checks each task's work: Claude's by GPT, or GPT's by Claude. The lead fixes each finding or sets it aside with its reason, and you decide what merges. Review is optional.

One board

Up next, running, needs you, settled: every task in the project, whichever lab's agent has it. Finished work waits in Needs you with its diff, its checks and screenshots of it working.

Switch plans mid-task

Althar runs the agents under your own sign-ins. When one plan runs out of usage, another account you're signed in to carries on, on the same thread and the same branch, unless the project keeps to its first.

Automations

Work that starts itself, at set times or every hour, such as a review of each new pull request. It runs on your computer while Althar is open, once you turn it on.

Skills, set up once

Add a skill once, and Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode all get it, in the roles and projects you pick. MCP servers work the same way.

Canvases

Leads draw pages, mockups and diagrams. Comment on a version, and the next one answers it.

Voice

Dictate to the coordinator or any task, transcribed on your computer.

Always in reach

Round the notch or in the menu bar on a Mac, in the tray on Windows and Linux: answer a permission or open a pull request without leaving what you're in.

Also in the box:

  • Ten at once. Each task gets a worktree of its own, so no two agents work in the same files. Each lead settles its own conflicts; only the odd one needs you.
  • See it running. Run the project from the window, with no agent. The page a task builds opens beside it, in a browser session of its own, and the lead tries its work there.
  • A task as a graph. A lane for each agent and a card for each step, round after round until the review passes.
  • Review pull requests. Paste a pull request's link and ask: a lead reads a copy of it, runs nothing of it, and drafts a review you post in one press.
  • Presets. Start work as a chat, a prototype, a small change, a full change or a pull request review, and change any part of it later, such as its reviewer or how it ends, by saying so.
  • Your tracker. Issues come in from Linear, Jira, Trello or GitHub; pull requests go out to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
  • Merge line. Pull requests merge one at a time, in the order you asked, or through the host's own merge queue.
  • Asks only before what can't be undone. Agents work without asking about each command; a force push or a push to the default branch waits for you. Your project's rules can ask about more.

Bring the agents you already pay for.

Althar runs each one under your own sign-in: your Claude plan, your ChatGPT plan, your keys. No new account, no new bill, nothing of ours between you and the model.

Switch labs whenever you like: your projects, their history and their decisions stay with you, on your computer.

The agents below are built in. Soon, other agents that speak the Agent Client Protocol will join from Settings too.


Claude Code
Claude Pro or Max, or an API key
Codex
ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Business, or an API key
GitHub Copilot
Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business or Enterprise
OpenCode
Any API key, or a local model
Junie
JetBrains AI Pro or Ultimate, or a Junie key

Grok Build
SuperGrok or X Premium+, or an xAI key
Kimi Code
A Kimi Code membership
Mistral Vibe
Le Chat Pro or Team, or a Mistral key
Qwen Code
Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan, or any API key
Google Antigravity
A Google account, signed in inside Althar

More on the way
Other ACP agents, from the ACP registry, such as Cursor, Gemini CLI or Goose, or your own command, once each passes a check that it asks before it acts (which, and why)

How it compares

If you use Such as Althar is
A terminal manager cmux
Claude Squad 		A project you talk to, not a grid of terminals to watch.
A chat app for agents T3 Code
Conductor 		A coordinator that splits the work into tasks and hands them out, not chats you start and keep up with yourself.
An agent harness or workflow engine Archon
Ruflo 		An app you tell what you want, not workflows or swarms to set up and run yourself.
An agent platform in its maker's cloud Amp
Devin 		On your computer: your projects and their history stay there, and there's no Althar account.
A lab's own app, or one a lab owns Claude app
ChatGPT app (Codex)
Cursor (SpaceX) 		Every lab's agents, on the plans you already pay for, one able to review another's work.
An AI editor Zed
VS Code with Copilot 		Where you manage the work, not an editor with an agent beside your code.

Get started

Note

Early-ish. Althar runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, and is tested most on macOS and Linux. Things will change, and some will break. Tell us when they do, or, in the app, Report a problem (in Help on a Mac, or at the foot of the quick settings), which sends what happened with the app's logs, paths and repository names hidden. Crash reports go on their own, masked the same way and never with your code, until you turn them off on the first screen or in Settings.

Download it for your system: a .dmg for macOS, the installer for Windows, or an AppImage, .deb or .rpm for Linux. On a Mac you can use Homebrew instead:

brew install --cask altharide/tap/althar

Open it. The first screen finds the agents on your computer and signs in the ones that aren't yet, each with its own sign-in. Then you pick the repositories your first project works in.

Copilot signs in inside Althar, for personal and work accounts, with no Copilot CLI to install; your organization's application and model policies still apply.

Want a hand getting set up? Book 20 minutes with me: althar.ai/office-hours. To build it from source instead, see DEVELOPMENT.md.

Learn more
Development Set up, run, test and change the code
Engineering standards What every app and package in the repository holds to
Architecture How Althar is built: a local-first desktop app, with seams for a later cloud
Decisions What has been decided, and why
Open questions What hasn't been decided yet
Glossary The words the interface uses: project, coordinator, task, lead, step
Thesis What happens to software engineering once coding agents are abundant
Components The interface, piece by piece, with every state as a story
Brand The mark, lockups, banners, screenshots and the characters

Contributing

The most useful thing you can do right now is use Althar on real work and tell us what breaks, in an issue. To change the code, start with CONTRIBUTING.md. Everyone taking part follows the code of conduct. To report a security problem, see SECURITY.md.

content_html_zh:
Stop babysitting tabs and terminals. Tell Althar's coordinator what you want. It puts agents to work, can have a model from another lab review them, and brings you back finished work, with the proof.

Download · Website · Get started · Contributing

Open source · Your own agents and plans · Runs on your computer · macOS, Windows and Linux

特征

Coordinator Tell it what you want, as you would a project manager. It knows your repositories, rules and past decisions, splits the work into tasks, picks an agent and a model to lead each, and starts them unless you change or hold it.
Review by another lab A model from another lab checks each task's work: Claude's by GPT, or GPT's by Claude. The lead fixes each finding or sets it aside with its reason, and you decide what merges. Review is optional.
One board Up next, running, needs you, settled: every task in the project, whichever lab's agent has it. Finished work waits in Needs you with its diff, its checks and screenshots of it working.
Switch plans mid-task Althar runs the agents under your own sign-ins. When one plan runs out of usage, another account you're signed in to carries on, on the same thread and the same branch, unless the project keeps to its first.
Automations Work that starts itself, at set times or every hour, such as a review of each new pull request. It runs on your computer while Althar is open, once you turn it on.
Skills, set up once Add a skill once, and Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode all get it, in the roles and projects you pick. MCP servers work the same way.
Canvases Leads draw pages, mockups and diagrams. Comment on a version, and the next one answers it.
Voice Dictate to the coordinator or any task, transcribed on your computer.
Always in reach Round the notch or in the menu bar on a Mac, in the tray on Windows and Linux: answer a permission or open a pull request without leaving what you're in.

Also in the box:

  • Ten at once. Each task gets a worktree of its own, so no two agents work in the same files. Each lead settles its own conflicts; only the odd one needs you.
  • See it running. Run the project from the window, with no agent. The page a task builds opens beside it, in a browser session of its own, and the lead tries its work there.
  • A task as a graph. A lane for each agent and a card for each step, round after round until the review passes.
  • Review pull requests. Paste a pull request's link and ask: a lead reads a copy of it, runs nothing of it, and drafts a review you post in one press.
  • Presets. Start work as a chat, a prototype, a small change, a full change or a pull request review, and change any part of it later, such as its reviewer or how it ends, by saying so.
  • Your tracker. Issues come in from Linear, Jira, Trello or GitHub; pull requests go out to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
  • Merge line. Pull requests merge one at a time, in the order you asked, or through the host's own merge queue.
  • Asks only before what can't be undone. Agents work without asking about each command; a force push or a push to the default branch waits for you. Your project's rules can ask about more.

Bring the agents you already pay for.

Althar runs each one under your own sign-in: your Claude plan, your ChatGPT plan, your keys. No new account, no new bill, nothing of ours between you and the model.

Switch labs whenever you like: your projects, their history and their decisions stay with you, on your computer.

The agents below are built in. Soon, other agents that speak the Agent Client Protocol will join from Settings too.

Claude Code Claude Pro or Max, or an API key Codex ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Business, or an API key GitHub Copilot Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business or Enterprise OpenCode Any API key, or a local model Junie JetBrains AI Pro or Ultimate, or a Junie key
Grok Build SuperGrok or X Premium+, or an xAI key Kimi Code A Kimi Code membership Mistral Vibe Le Chat Pro or Team, or a Mistral key Qwen Code Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan, or any API key Google Antigravity A Google account, signed in inside Althar
More on the way Other ACP agents, from the ACP registry, such as Cursor, Gemini CLI or Goose, or your own command, once each passes a check that it asks before it acts (which, and why)

比较如何

If you use Such as Althar is
A terminal manager cmux Claude Squad A project you talk to, not a grid of terminals to watch.
A chat app for agents T3 Code Conductor A coordinator that splits the work into tasks and hands them out, not chats you start and keep up with yourself.
An agent harness or workflow engine Archon Ruflo An app you tell what you want, not workflows or swarms to set up and run yourself.
An agent platform in its maker's cloud Amp Devin On your computer: your projects and their history stay there, and there's no Althar account.
A lab's own app, or one a lab owns Claude app ChatGPT app (Codex) Cursor (SpaceX) Every lab's agents, on the plans you already pay for, one able to review another's work.
An AI editor Zed VS Code with Copilot Where you manage the work, not an editor with an agent beside your code.

开始使用

Note

Early-ish. Althar runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, and is tested most on macOS and Linux. Things will change, and some will break. Tell us when they do, or, in the app, Report a problem (in Help on a Mac, or at the foot of the quick settings), which sends what happened with the app's logs, paths and repository names hidden. Crash reports go on their own, masked the same way and never with your code, until you turn them off on the first screen or in Settings.

Download it for your system: a .dmg for macOS, the installer for Windows, or an AppImage, .deb or .rpm for Linux. On a Mac you can use Homebrew instead:

brew install --cask altharide/tap/althar

Open it. The first screen finds the agents on your computer and signs in the ones that aren't yet, each with its own sign-in. Then you pick the repositories your first project works in.

Copilot signs in inside Althar, for personal and work accounts, with no Copilot CLI to install; your organization's application and model policies still apply.

Want a hand getting set up? Book 20 minutes with me: althar.ai/office-hours. To build it from source instead, see DEVELOPMENT.md.
